nodes.label: Agent Orchestration and Multi-Agent Exploitation
nodes.text: Attacks targeting coordination mechanisms between agents

nodes.label: Agent Supply Chain and Dependency Risk
nodes.text: Compromised models, libraries, or third-party tools

nodes.label: Agent Untraceability
nodes.text: Inability to audit agent decision chains or attribute actions

nodes.label: Agentic AI Tool Misuse
nodes.text: Compromised tool selection, insecure invocation, or lack of oversight

nodes.label: Insecure Agent Critical Systems Interaction
nodes.text: Unauthorized manipulation of infrastructure, IoT, or operational technology

nodes.label: LLM01:25 - Prompt Injection
nodes.text: This manipulates a large language model (LLM) through crafty inputs, causing unintended actions by the LLM. Direct injections overwrite system prompts, while indirect ones manipulate inputs from external sources.

nodes.label: LLM02:25 - Sensitive Information Disclosure
nodes.text: Sensitive info in LLMs includes PII, financial, health, business, security, and legal data. Proprietary models face risks with unique training methods and source code, critical in closed or foundation models.

nodes.label: LLM03:25 - Supply Chain
nodes.text: LLM supply chains face risks in training data, models, and platforms, causing bias, breaches, or failures. Unlike traditional software, ML risks include third-party pre-trained models and data vulnerabilities.

nodes.label: LLM04:25 - Data and Model Poisoning
nodes.text: Data poisoning manipulates pre-training, fine-tuning, or embedding data, causing vulnerabilities, biases, or backdoors. Risks include degraded performance, harmful outputs, toxic content, and compromised downstream systems.

nodes.label: LLM05:25 - Improper Output Handling
nodes.text: Improper Output Handling involves inadequate validation of LLM outputs before downstream use. Exploits include XSS, CSRF, SSRF, privilege escalation, or remote code execution, which differs from Overreliance.

nodes.label: LLM06:25 - Excessive Agency
nodes.text: LLM systems gain agency via extensions, tools, or plugins to act on prompts. Agents dynamically choose extensions and make repeated LLM calls, using prior outputs to guide subsequent actions for dynamic task execution.

nodes.label: LLM07:25 - System Prompt Leakage
nodes.text: System prompt leakage occurs when sensitive info in LLM prompts is unintentionally exposed, enabling attackers to exploit secrets. These prompts guide model behavior but can unintentionally reveal critical data.

nodes.label: LLM08:25 - Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
nodes.text: Vectors and embeddings vulnerabilities in RAG with LLMs allow exploits via weak generation, storage, or retrieval. These can inject harmful content, manipulate outputs, or expose sensitive data, posing significant security risks.

nodes.label: LLM09:25 - Misinformation
nodes.text: LLM misinformation occurs when false and credible outputs mislead users, risking security breaches, reputational harm, and legal liability, making it a critical vulnerability for reliant applications.

nodes.label: LLM10:25 - Unbounded Consumption
nodes.text: Unbounded Consumption occurs when LLMs generate outputs from inputs, relying on inference to apply learned patterns and knowledge for relevant responses or predictions, making it a key function of LLMs.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A002: Establish output data policy / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:A002: Establish output data policy / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Implementing technical controls to enforce AI output opt-in/opt-out and deletion policies. For example, automating customer preference enforcement through consent management configuration, processing opt-out and deletion requests within defined workflows, and validating that opted-out outputs are excluded from storage and downstream reuse.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A002: Establish output data policy / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:A002: Establish output data policy / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A002: Establish output data policy / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:A002: Establish output data policy / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Establishing output ownership and usage rights policies. For example, specifying customer ownership of AI-generated outputs versus AI inputs, defining permitted uses of outputs (commercial use, redistribution, modification), documenting usage restrictions or limitations, and clarifying how ownership applies to different output types or use cases.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A002: Establish output data policy / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:A002: Establish output data policy / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Disclosing opt-in/opt-out and deletion policies for AI outputs. For example, documenting how customers can opt out of output storage or reuse, explaining deletion request processes, specifying retention periods and data handling practices, and clarifying how customers can control or revoke permissions for their outputs.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A003: Limit AI agent data access / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:A003: Limit AI agent data access / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Enabling agent identity management. For example, assigning each agent a unique, cryptographically verifiable identity; supporting standard identity federation protocols (e.g., OAuth 2.0, OIDC) for enterprise IAM integration; publishing agent cards declaring each agent's capabilities, tools, and permission scopes.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A003: Limit AI agent data access / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:A003: Limit AI agent data access / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Enabling agent access and governance through permission-ready architecture. For example, exposing per-agent permission scopes mappable to enterprise roles; supporting just-in-time permissions scoped to specific subtasks; preventing silent inheritance of elevated permissions from orchestrators or parent agents; enforcing segregation of duties across systems; and integrating data loss prevention controls on agent actions and tool calls.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A003: Limit AI agent data access / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:A003: Limit AI agent data access / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A003: Limit AI agent data access / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:A003: Limit AI agent data access / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Configuring data access limits to reduce data and privacy exposure. For example, limiting data access to task-relevant information based on context, implementing scoping based on user roles or workflow requirements, and avoiding persistent or out-of-scope data access.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A004: Protect IP & trade secrets / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:A004: Protect IP & trade secrets / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Leveraging foundation model provider protections. For example, using providers with zero data retention policies, requiring contractual commitments that inputs are not used for training, selecting models with enhanced privacy guarantees for sensitive use cases.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A004: Protect IP & trade secrets / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:A004: Protect IP & trade secrets / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Implementing technical controls to detect proprietary information in outputs.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A004: Protect IP & trade secrets / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:A004: Protect IP & trade secrets / Control mays/3
nodes.text: Establishing output monitoring for high-risk IP scenarios. For example, logging AI responses that accessed confidential data sources, implementing human review workflows for outputs flagged as potentially containing sensitive information.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A004: Protect IP & trade secrets / Control mays/4
nodes.label: blk:A004: Protect IP & trade secrets / Control mays/4

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A004: Protect IP & trade secrets / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:A004: Protect IP & trade secrets / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Providing user guidance on protecting confidential information. For example, instructing employees not to input trade secrets, proprietary code, or confidential business information into AI systems, communicating data handling policies for AI tool usage, or establishing clear guidelines on what information can and cannot be shared with AI agents.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A005: Prevent cross-customer data exposure / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:A005: Prevent cross-customer data exposure / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Implementing specific privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) to reduce competitive exposure.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A005: Prevent cross-customer data exposure / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:A005: Prevent cross-customer data exposure / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A005: Prevent cross-customer data exposure / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:A005: Prevent cross-customer data exposure / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Establishing explicit consent and disclosure for combined data usage. For example, informing customers when their data will be combined with competitor data, disclosing data anonymization and abstraction policies, providing opt-out mechanisms.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A005: Prevent cross-customer data exposure / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:A005: Prevent cross-customer data exposure / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing customer data isolation controls. For example, enforcing strict logical and physical separation of customer data, applying tenant-specific encryption, validating data flow boundaries in shared infrastructure, establishing technical barriers between customer datasets during training.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A006: Prevent PII leakage / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:A006: Prevent PII leakage / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Integrating with existing data loss prevention (DLP) systems to monitor and block outputs containing personal data in violation of policy.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A006: Prevent PII leakage / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:A006: Prevent PII leakage / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A006: Prevent PII leakage / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:A006: Prevent PII leakage / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing safeguards to prevent personal data leakage through AI system outputs and logs. For example, filtering prompts and outputs for personal identifiers before storage or display, implementing automated PII detection and redaction in system logs, preventing retention of outputs containing sensitive personal information, or blocking responses that would expose personal identifiers.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A007: Prevent IP violations / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:A007: Prevent IP violations / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Establishing supplementary content filtering mechanisms where provider protections have gaps or limitations. For example, detecting copyrighted material in outputs, implementing trademark screening.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A007: Prevent IP violations / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:A007: Prevent IP violations / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Implementing user guidance and guardrails to reduce IP risk. For example, usage policies that explain prohibited content types, user warnings in product, restricting output generation in known infringement domains.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A007: Prevent IP violations / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:A007: Prevent IP violations / Control mays/3
nodes.text: Implementing restrictions in AI acceptable use policy.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A007: Prevent IP violations / Control mays/4
nodes.label: blk:A007: Prevent IP violations / Control mays/4

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A007: Prevent IP violations / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:A007: Prevent IP violations / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Documenting foundation model provider IP protections which may serve as primary infringement safeguards. For example, indemnification clauses or copyright/trademark guardrails.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A008: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:A008: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Implementing user-facing warnings when potential secrets are detected in user inputs. For example, alerting users when credentials are detected in their prompts.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A008: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:A008: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Implementing safeguards to prevent secrets from being retained in platform logs, conversation history, and stored artifacts. For example, redacting detected credential patterns before log storage, masking secrets in conversation history displayed to users or support staff, or applying scrubbing functions to prompts and outputs before persistence.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A008: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:A008: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A008: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:A008: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing safeguards to detect credentials in user inputs. For example, scanning user prompts and pasted content for API keys, access tokens, private keys, and connection strings using pattern-matching or entropy-based detection; defining handling procedures when detected such as warning the user, refusing to persist, or flagging to the deployer.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A008: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:A008: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing safeguards to keep secrets out of generated code artifacts. For example, guiding the model via system prompts to reference environment variables or secret-management tools rather than hardcoding credentials, post-generation scanning of output files for common credential patterns, or blocking/flagging generations that contain detected secrets before they are written to disk.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:A008: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:A008: Prevent leakage of credentials and secrets / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Implementing safeguards to securely store user-provided credentials to enable agent-connected services. For example, storing OAuth tokens, API keys, and connection strings in a dedicated secret manager, encrypting credentials at rest, scoping credential access per tool and per session, or fetching credentials only at the point of tool invocation rather than persisting them in the agent's context window.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B001: Third-party testing of adversarial robustness / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:B001: Third-party testing of adversarial robustness / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Aligning adversarial testing with broader security testing programs. For example, integrating AI-specific test cases into broader penetration testing, sharing threat models across red/blue teams, aligning test cycles with security audit and compliance calendars.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B001: Third-party testing of adversarial robustness / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:B001: Third-party testing of adversarial robustness / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B001: Third-party testing of adversarial robustness / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:B001: Third-party testing of adversarial robustness / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Establishing a taxonomy for adversarial risks. For example, drawing on NIST's AI 100-2e2023 attack classifications and aligning these to system architecture and use cases.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B001: Third-party testing of adversarial robustness / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:B001: Third-party testing of adversarial robustness / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Conducting comprehensive adversarial testing at least quarterly. For example, performing structured red-teaming, prompt injection assessments, jailbreaking attempts, adversarial perturbation testing, semantic manipulation, and simulated malicious tool invocations.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B001: Third-party testing of adversarial robustness / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:B001: Third-party testing of adversarial robustness / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Maintaining secure testing documentation. For example, recording test cases, methods, outcomes, and system behaviors with restricted access controls, implementing secure storage for sensitive testing materials.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B001: Third-party testing of adversarial robustness / Control shoulds/4
nodes.label: blk:B001: Third-party testing of adversarial robustness / Control shoulds/4
nodes.text: Establishing improvement processes based on findings. For example, assigning owners and remediation timelines based on test severity, tracking fixes through risk registers or issue management systems, documenting updates to safeguards and procedures.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B002: Detect adversarial input / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:B002: Detect adversarial input / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Implementing adversarial input detection prior to AI model processing where feasible. For example, using pre-processing filters to flag likely threats before model processing.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B002: Detect adversarial input / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:B002: Detect adversarial input / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Integrating adversarial input detection into existing security operations tooling. For example, forwarding flagged inputs to SIEM platforms, correlating detection with authentication and network logs, enabling SOC teams to triage AI-related security events.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B002: Detect adversarial input / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:B002: Detect adversarial input / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B002: Detect adversarial input / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:B002: Detect adversarial input / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Establishing detection and alerting. For example, implementing monitoring for prompt injection patterns, jailbreak techniques, adversarial input attempts, and exceeding rate limits, configuring alerts and threat notifications for suspicious activities.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B002: Detect adversarial input / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:B002: Detect adversarial input / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing incident logging and response procedures. For example, logging suspected adversarial attacks with relevant context, escalating to designated personnel based on severity, and documenting response actions in a centralized system.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B002: Detect adversarial input / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:B002: Detect adversarial input / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Maintaining detection effectiveness through quarterly reviews. For example, updating detection rules based on emerging adversarial techniques, analyzing incident patterns and documenting system improvements.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B003: Manage public release of technical details / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:B003: Manage public release of technical details / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Establishing approval processes. For example, requiring designated review for public content referencing AI capabilities in e.g. publications, presentations, and marketing materials, and documenting approved disclosures with business justification.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B003: Manage public release of technical details / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:B003: Manage public release of technical details / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B003: Manage public release of technical details / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:B003: Manage public release of technical details / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Documenting limitations on technical information release. For example, limiting public disclosure of model architectures, algorithms, training data details, system configurations, and performance metrics, requiring approval before sharing technical specifications or implementation details.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B003: Manage public release of technical details / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:B003: Manage public release of technical details / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Controlling organizational information to balance transparency with security. For example, limiting disclosure of AI team details, development timelines, and other information that could reveal technical capabilities, reviewing public communications for sensitive information.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B004: Prevent AI endpoint scraping / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:B004: Prevent AI endpoint scraping / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing systems distinguishing between high-volume legitimate usage and adversarial behavior. For example, using behavioral analytics and user profiling to calibrate detection thresholds and prevent false positives against trusted users.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B004: Prevent AI endpoint scraping / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:B004: Prevent AI endpoint scraping / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing rate limiting and query restrictions. For example, establishing per-user quotas to prevent model extraction, blocking excessive query patterns, implementing progressive restrictions for suspicious behavior, or using economic disincentives for high-volume usage.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B004: Prevent AI endpoint scraping / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:B004: Prevent AI endpoint scraping / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Conducting simulated external attack testing of AI endpoints. For example, performing automated attack simulations, testing endpoint protection effectiveness against high-volume and distributed attacks, and documenting methodologies appropriate to organizational threat profile.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B004: Prevent AI endpoint scraping / Control shoulds/4
nodes.label: blk:B004: Prevent AI endpoint scraping / Control shoulds/4
nodes.text: Maintaining endpoint security through remediation. For example, tracking identified vulnerabilities, implementing protective measures based on testing outcomes, and regularly updating endpoint defenses and detection thresholds.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B004: Prevent AI endpoint scraping / Control shoulds/5
nodes.label: blk:B004: Prevent AI endpoint scraping / Control shoulds/5

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B005: Implement real-time input filtering / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:B005: Implement real-time input filtering / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Documenting the moderation logic and rationale. For example, explaining chosen moderation tools, threshold justifications, and decision criteria for different risk categories.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B005: Implement real-time input filtering / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:B005: Implement real-time input filtering / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Providing feedback to users when inputs are blocked.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B005: Implement real-time input filtering / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:B005: Implement real-time input filtering / Control mays/3
nodes.text: Logging flagged prompts for analysis and refinement of filters, while ensuring compliance with privacy obligations.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B005: Implement real-time input filtering / Control mays/4
nodes.label: blk:B005: Implement real-time input filtering / Control mays/4
nodes.text: Periodically evaluating filter performance and adjusting thresholds accordingly. For example, accuracy, latency, false positives/negatives.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B005: Implement real-time input filtering / Control mays/5
nodes.label: blk:B005: Implement real-time input filtering / Control mays/5

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B005: Implement real-time input filtering / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:B005: Implement real-time input filtering / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Integrating automated moderation tools to filter inputs before they reach the foundation model. For example, integrating third-party moderation APIs, implementing custom filtering rules, configuring blocking or warning actions for flagged content, and establishing confidence thresholds based on risk category and severity.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B006: Prevent unauthorized AI agent actions / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:B006: Prevent unauthorized AI agent actions / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Implementing additional safeguards to contain runtime risk. For example, enabling sandboxed execution environments with configurable filesystem, network, and credential restrictions for agent-executed code and first-party MCP servers, monitoring MCP tool definitions for unauthorized changes after initial approval, providing pre-execution authorization hooks that verify runtime tool calls against defined policy before execution proceeds, or scanning agent configuration artifacts such as hooks, skills and rules for prompt injection or unauthorized behavior.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B006: Prevent unauthorized AI agent actions / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:B006: Prevent unauthorized AI agent actions / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B006: Prevent unauthorized AI agent actions / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:B006: Prevent unauthorized AI agent actions / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing technical restrictions that limit agent capabilities to authorized scope. For example, restricting agent access to approved backend services, APIs and MCP servers, enforcing network segmentation or API gateway rules, or implementing service-level authorization preventing access to sensitive systems.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B006: Prevent unauthorized AI agent actions / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:B006: Prevent unauthorized AI agent actions / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Deploying monitoring and alerting for agent actions that exceed security boundaries. For example, logging all agent service interactions, alerting on access attempts to unauthorized systems or APIs, or anomaly detection flagging unusual connection patterns.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B007: Enforce user access privileges to AI systems / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:B007: Enforce user access privileges to AI systems / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing system-level access controls tailored to AI systems. For example, using role-based or attribute-based access to restrict access to model configuration, training datasets, tool-calling capabilities, or prompt logs, based on job function and system sensitivity.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B007: Enforce user access privileges to AI systems / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:B007: Enforce user access privileges to AI systems / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Restricting administrative and configuration privileges to authorized personnel. For example, limiting ability to alter system behavior, tools, or models.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B007: Enforce user access privileges to AI systems / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:B007: Enforce user access privileges to AI systems / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Conducting access reviews and updates at least quarterly. For example, validating access assignments, updating based on policy or role changes,  documenting access changes with AI-specific context (e.g. model access justification, changes to agent capability boundaries, or access to sensitive prompt/response history).

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B007: Enforce user access privileges to AI systems / Control shoulds/4
nodes.label: blk:B007: Enforce user access privileges to AI systems / Control shoulds/4

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B008: Protect AI system deployment environment / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:B008: Protect AI system deployment environment / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Enforcing data integrity across agentic interfaces. For example, implementing cryptographic message signing for agent-to-agent communication; applying schema validation and input sanitization to MCP tool call inputs and outputs.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B008: Protect AI system deployment environment / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:B008: Protect AI system deployment environment / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Securing model hosting environments. For example, using up-to-date and minimal container images, scanning for known vulnerabilities in dependencies and base images, and applying infrastructure-level isolation techniques based on risk level (e.g. container namespaces, VM separation, or dedicated GPU access).

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B008: Protect AI system deployment environment / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:B008: Protect AI system deployment environment / Control mays/3
nodes.text: Verifying model integrity before and during deployment. For example, using cryptographic checksums or signed artifacts to detect tampering, scanning model files for malicious payloads.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B008: Protect AI system deployment environment / Control mays/4
nodes.label: blk:B008: Protect AI system deployment environment / Control mays/4

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B008: Protect AI system deployment environment / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:B008: Protect AI system deployment environment / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Enforcing caller authentication across API endpoints and agentic interfaces. For example, applying scoped API tokens or signed requests for model API access; enforcing OAuth 2.0 or OIDC token validation with appropriate scoping for MCP server connections; implementing mutual authentication for agent-to-agent interfaces.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B008: Protect AI system deployment environment / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:B008: Protect AI system deployment environment / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Securing data in transit across model API endpoints and agentic interfaces. For example, enforcing TLS for all model API endpoint traffic, MCP server connections, and agent-to-agent communication channels; implementing credential rotation policies for long-lived service connections.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B009: Limit output over-exposure / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:B009: Limit output over-exposure / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Providing user-facing notices or documentation about output limitations.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B009: Limit output over-exposure / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:B009: Limit output over-exposure / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Limiting the fidelity of model outputs in certain use cases. For example, applying output rounding, threshold bands, or obfuscation techniques to reduce the risk of model inversion.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B009: Limit output over-exposure / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:B009: Limit output over-exposure / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B009: Limit output over-exposure / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:B009: Limit output over-exposure / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Reducing or limiting the number of results shown in outputs to relevant only to balance security and utility. For example, character limits, limits on inference time.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Implementing safeguards to promote secure defaults for session management in generated code. For example, applying HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite flags to session cookies by default, or defaulting to CSRF protections on state-changing endpoints.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Implementing safeguards to promote defensive programming patterns in generated code. For example, defaulting to input validation on user-supplied data, applying safe error handling that avoids exposing stack traces or internal details, or defaulting to rate limiting on generated public-facing endpoints.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control mays/3
nodes.text: Implementing safeguards to prevent generated logging code from capturing secrets or personal information. For example, defaulting logging patterns to exclude sensitive fields, or applying guidance that avoids logging full request bodies or auth headers.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control mays/4
nodes.label: blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control mays/4

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing safeguards to promote secure patterns for common web vulnerability classes in generated code. For example, defaulting to parameterized queries or safe ORM patterns for database access, applying output encoding and contextual escaping to prevent cross-site scripting, or enforcing HTTPS/TLS in generated network and API code.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing safeguards to promote secure patterns for authentication and authorization in generated code. For example, defaulting to vetted authentication libraries or patterns on auth-related prompts, applying access control checks and least-privilege patterns by default, or avoiding generation of custom cryptographic or authentication primitives.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:B010: Promote secure patterns in generated code / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Implementing safeguards to prevent dependency risks in generated code. For example, avoiding wildcard version specifications (e.g., * or latest) in generated manifests, verifying that suggested packages exist in their respective registries before including them in generated code, or applying guidance that avoids known-abandoned or typosquatted packages.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C001: Define AI risk taxonomy / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:C001: Define AI risk taxonomy / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Defining risk categories with severity levels and examples based on industry and deployment context. For example, classifying harmful outputs such as distressed outputs, angry responses, high-risk advice, offensive content, bias, and deception, identifying other high-risk use cases such as safety-critical instructions, legal recommendations, financial advice.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C001: Define AI risk taxonomy / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:C001: Define AI risk taxonomy / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Aligning risk taxonomy with external frameworks and standards.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C001: Define AI risk taxonomy / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:C001: Define AI risk taxonomy / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Establishing severity grading appropriate to organizational context and risk tolerance. For example, implementing consistent scoring methodology across risk categories, defining thresholds for flagging and human review.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C001: Define AI risk taxonomy / Control shoulds/4
nodes.label: blk:C001: Define AI risk taxonomy / Control shoulds/4
nodes.text: Maintaining taxonomy currency with documented change management. For example, updating based on emerging threats or incidents.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C001: Define AI risk taxonomy / Control shoulds/5
nodes.label: blk:C001: Define AI risk taxonomy / Control shoulds/5

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C002: Conduct pre-deployment testing / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:C002: Conduct pre-deployment testing / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Integrating AI system testing into established software development lifecycle (SDLC) gates. For example, including threat modelling and risk evaluation during design phases, requiring risk evaluation and sign-off at staging or pre-production milestones, aligning with CI/CD or MLOps pipelines, and documenting test artefacts in shared repositories."

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C002: Conduct pre-deployment testing / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:C002: Conduct pre-deployment testing / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Implementing pre-deployment vulnerability scanning of AI artifacts and dependencies. For example, scanning AI models and ML libraries for security vulnerabilities, validating runtime behavior for unsafe operations, and analyzing outputs for harmful content before deployment.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C002: Conduct pre-deployment testing / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:C002: Conduct pre-deployment testing / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C002: Conduct pre-deployment testing / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:C002: Conduct pre-deployment testing / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Conducting pre-deployment testing with documented results and identified issues. For example, structured hallucination testing, adversarial prompting, safety unit tests, and scenario-based walkthroughs.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C002: Conduct pre-deployment testing / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:C002: Conduct pre-deployment testing / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Completing risk assessments of identified issues before system deployment. For example, potential impact analysis, mitigation strategies, and residual risk evaluation.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C002: Conduct pre-deployment testing / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:C002: Conduct pre-deployment testing / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Obtaining approval sign-offs from designated accountable. For example, documented rationale for approval decisions and maintained records for review purposes.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C003: Prevent harmful outputs / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:C003: Prevent harmful outputs / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Implementing bias detection and mitigation controls. For example, monitoring for discriminatory patterns, implementing fairness checks in outputs.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C003: Prevent harmful outputs / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:C003: Prevent harmful outputs / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Evaluating harm mitigation controls using performance metrics.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C003: Prevent harmful outputs / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:C003: Prevent harmful outputs / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C003: Prevent harmful outputs / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:C003: Prevent harmful outputs / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing content filtering for harmful output types. For example, detecting and blocking distressed responses, angry language, offensive content, biased statements, and deceptive information.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C003: Prevent harmful outputs / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:C003: Prevent harmful outputs / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing guardrails for advice generation. For example, restricting high-risk recommendations in sensitive domains, requiring disclaimers for guidance.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C004: Prevent out-of-scope outputs / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:C004: Prevent out-of-scope outputs / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Providing user guidance on system capabilities and limitations. For example, communicating what the AI system can and cannot do, intended use cases, and topics or requests outside the system's scope.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C004: Prevent out-of-scope outputs / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:C004: Prevent out-of-scope outputs / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C004: Prevent out-of-scope outputs / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:C004: Prevent out-of-scope outputs / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Detecting and blocking out-of-scope requests. For example, detecting conversations outside intended use cases, blocking prohibited topics, providing redirection messages when users hit boundaries, and escalating or restricting access for repeated violations.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C004: Prevent out-of-scope outputs / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:C004: Prevent out-of-scope outputs / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Tracking out-of-scope violations and updating boundaries. For example, logging boundary violations, adjusting restrictions based on misuse patterns.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C005: Prevent agent-specific high risk outputs / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:C005: Prevent agent-specific high risk outputs / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Establishing escalation procedures for flagged high-risk content. For example, defining when human review is required and establishing approval workflows for edge cases.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C005: Prevent agent-specific high risk outputs / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:C005: Prevent agent-specific high risk outputs / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Implementing automated real-time interventions. For example, blocking or modifying outputs based on severity.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C005: Prevent agent-specific high risk outputs / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:C005: Prevent agent-specific high risk outputs / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C005: Prevent agent-specific high risk outputs / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:C005: Prevent agent-specific high risk outputs / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing detection and blocking mechanisms aligned with organizational risk taxonomy. For example, deploying filtering based on defined risk categories and severity thresholds.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C005: Prevent agent-specific high risk outputs / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:C005: Prevent agent-specific high risk outputs / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing response actions for detected risks. For example, blocking high-severity outputs, flagging medium-risk content for review, logging violations for monitoring and analysis.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C006: Prevent output vulnerabilities / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:C006: Prevent output vulnerabilities / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Detecting advanced output-based attack patterns. For example, identifying prompt injection attempts, model subversion techniques, payloads targeting downstream systems, or obfuscated exploits designed to bypass filters.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C006: Prevent output vulnerabilities / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:C006: Prevent output vulnerabilities / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C006: Prevent output vulnerabilities / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:C006: Prevent output vulnerabilities / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Establishing output sanitization and validation procedures before presenting content to users. For example, encoding or stripping potentially malicious content, validating structured outputs against safe schemas, blocking unsafe URLs, and enforcing secure rendering modes.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C006: Prevent output vulnerabilities / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:C006: Prevent output vulnerabilities / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing content handling and security labelling based on trust level. For example, marking untrusted or third-party content, distinguishing external data from system-generated content, and applying differentiated security controls based on content source.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C007: Flag high risk outputs for human review / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:C007: Flag high risk outputs for human review / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Establishing human review workflows for flagged high-risk outputs. For example, assigning reviewers, defining escalation procedures for complex cases, managing review queues with response time tracking, documenting review decisions, and reviewing workflow effectiveness regularly.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C007: Flag high risk outputs for human review / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:C007: Flag high risk outputs for human review / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C007: Flag high risk outputs for human review / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:C007: Flag high risk outputs for human review / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Defining high-risk output criteria drawing on risk taxonomy.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C007: Flag high risk outputs for human review / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:C007: Flag high risk outputs for human review / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing automated detection mechanisms for high-risk outputs. For example, using content filtering, risk scoring, or classification models to identify outputs requiring review or flagging.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C008: Monitor AI risk categories / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:C008: Monitor AI risk categories / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Maintaining documentation. For example, recording identified scenarios with clear examples, updating risk taxonomy based on monitoring findings and incidents.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C008: Monitor AI risk categories / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:C008: Monitor AI risk categories / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Integrating AI output monitoring with existing security tools. For example, forwarding alerts and flagged outputs to SIEM platforms, applying standard logging formats (e.g. JSON, syslog) to support automated threat detection workflows.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C008: Monitor AI risk categories / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:C008: Monitor AI risk categories / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C008: Monitor AI risk categories / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:C008: Monitor AI risk categories / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Establishing ongoing monitoring of AI outputs across risk categories. For example, conducting regular evaluations prioritized by risk severity, sampling outputs for review, and tracking system behavior patterns.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C009: Enable real-time feedback and intervention / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:C009: Enable real-time feedback and intervention / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Reviewing user feedback and intervention logs at regular intervals, analyzing findings using structured methodologies (e.g., categorizing by risk domain, frequency, and severity), and integrating corrective actions into product backlogs or compliance workflows, with records maintained for traceability.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C009: Enable real-time feedback and intervention / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:C009: Enable real-time feedback and intervention / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C009: Enable real-time feedback and intervention / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:C009: Enable real-time feedback and intervention / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Enabling user intervention capabilities. For example, providing mechanisms for users to pause, stop, or redirect system behavior, implementing feedback collection tools for users to report issues or concerns, ensuring technical controls persist across devices and interaction contexts.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C009: Enable real-time feedback and intervention / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:C009: Enable real-time feedback and intervention / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Ensuring accessibility of feedback and intervention mechanisms. For example, adhering to WCAG 2.1 standards for color contrast, screen reader compatibility, keyboard navigation, and clear messaging for users with disabilities.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C010: Third-party testing for harmful outputs / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:C010: Third-party testing for harmful outputs / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Appointing qualified third-party assessors. Including selecting assessors with relevant technical capabilities for identified risk areas, maintaining records of assessor qualifications and independence.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C010: Third-party testing for harmful outputs / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:C010: Third-party testing for harmful outputs / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Conducting regular testing. Including performing assessments of harmful outputs at least every quarter, defining testing scope and methodologies based on risk classifications and industry benchmarks like ToxiGen, coordinating with internal security and testing teams.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C010: Third-party testing for harmful outputs / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:C010: Third-party testing for harmful outputs / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Maintaining documentation. Including testing scope, results, and remediation actions taken, tracking follow-up activities and resolution timelines.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:C010: Third-party testing for harmful outputs / Control shoulds/4
nodes.label: blk:C010: Third-party testing for harmful outputs / Control shoulds/4

blk:Control mays/1
nodes.text: Documenting processes for handling end-user data subject rights. For example, handling requests for opt-in/opt-out rights, access, portability, or deletion of input data.

nodes.label: blk:Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Defining and communicating input data usage policies. Including specifying how customer data is used for inference and model training, establishing data retention periods, and documenting customer data rights.

nodes.label: blk:Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing technical controls to enforce data retention and deletion policies. For example, automating data deletion based on retention schedules, using secure removal mechanisms, and managing data lifecycles.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:D001: Prevent hallucinated outputs / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:D001: Prevent hallucinated outputs / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Maintaining uncertainty communication. For example, displaying confidence levels, providing appropriate disclaimers for generated information.

nodes.label: blk:D001: Prevent hallucinated outputs / Control mays/2

nodes.label: blk:D001: Prevent hallucinated outputs / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing factual accuracy controls. For example, deploying available fact-checking mechanisms, flagging uncertain or low-confidence responses.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:D001: Prevent hallucinated outputs / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:D001: Prevent hallucinated outputs / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Establishing information source validation. For example, requiring citations for factual claims, implementing source reliability checks.

nodes.text: Appointing qualified third-party assessors. Including selecting assessors with relevant technical capabilities for identified risk areas, maintaining records of assessor qualifications and independence.

nodes.label: blk:D002: Third-party testing for hallucinations / Control shoulds/2

nodes.label: blk:D002: Third-party testing for hallucinations / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Maintaining documentation. Including testing scope, results, and remediation actions taken, tracking follow-up activities and resolution timelines.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:D003: Restrict unsafe tool calls / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:D003: Restrict unsafe tool calls / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Requiring human approval for sensitive tool operations. For example, requiring human confirmation before executing high-risk actions, multi-step tool calls, implementing approval workflows for operations beyond autonomous boundaries.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:D003: Restrict unsafe tool calls / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:D003: Restrict unsafe tool calls / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Reviewing patterns of AI tool usage. For example, identifying anomalies, updating tool permissions, and retiring unused or high-risk functions during scheduled evaluations.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:D003: Restrict unsafe tool calls / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:D003: Restrict unsafe tool calls / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:D003: Restrict unsafe tool calls / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:D003: Restrict unsafe tool calls / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing tool call validation and authorization. For example, restricting tool calls to approved functions and MCP servers, validating parameters before execution.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:D003: Restrict unsafe tool calls / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:D003: Restrict unsafe tool calls / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Enforcing rate limits and transaction caps for autonomous tool use.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:D003: Restrict unsafe tool calls / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:D003: Restrict unsafe tool calls / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Establishing execution monitoring and logging. For example, tracking all tool calls, monitoring for unauthorized access attempts or scope violations.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:D004: Third-party testing of tool calls / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:D004: Third-party testing of tool calls / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Appointing qualified third-party assessors. Including selecting assessors with relevant technical capabilities for identified risk areas, maintaining records of assessor qualifications and independence.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:D004: Third-party testing of tool calls / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:D004: Third-party testing of tool calls / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Conducting regular testing. Including defining testing scope and methodologies based on risk taxonomy and performing assessments of tool calls at least every quarter.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:D004: Third-party testing of tool calls / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:D004: Third-party testing of tool calls / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Maintaining documentation. Including testing scope, results, and remediation actions taken, tracking follow-up activities and resolution timelines.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:D004: Third-party testing of tool calls / Control shoulds/4
nodes.label: blk:D004: Third-party testing of tool calls / Control shoulds/4

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E001: AI failure plan for security breaches / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E001: AI failure plan for security breaches / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Assigning a breach response lead from existing staff. For example, IT manager, security officer, or designated executive with authority to engage external counsel and specialists as needed.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E001: AI failure plan for security breaches / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E001: AI failure plan for security breaches / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Defining breach notification procedures. For example, customer communications, regulatory reporting requirements, and vendor notifications based on applicable privacy laws.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E001: AI failure plan for security breaches / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:E001: AI failure plan for security breaches / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Implementing security remediation measures. For example, system freeze capabilities, vulnerability fixes, access control updates, and coordination with external security consultants when internal expertise is insufficient.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E001: AI failure plan for security breaches / Control shoulds/4
nodes.label: blk:E001: AI failure plan for security breaches / Control shoulds/4
nodes.text: Establishing evidence collection requirements with guidance on preserving evidence for potential legal review. For example, system logs, user activity records, and basic documentation.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E001: AI failure plan for security breaches / Control shoulds/5
nodes.label: blk:E001: AI failure plan for security breaches / Control shoulds/5

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E002: AI failure plan for harmful outputs / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:E002: AI failure plan for harmful outputs / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Defining harmful output categories with reference to risk taxonomy. For example, discriminatory content, offensive material, inappropriate recommendations, ideally with concrete examples.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E002: AI failure plan for harmful outputs / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:E002: AI failure plan for harmful outputs / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Coordinating external support engagement. For example,  legal counsel consultation, PR support, and insurance claim procedures.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E002: AI failure plan for harmful outputs / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:E002: AI failure plan for harmful outputs / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E002: AI failure plan for harmful outputs / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E002: AI failure plan for harmful outputs / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing customer communication protocols. For example, disclosure procedures, explanation of corrective actions, and follow-up commitments with executive approval for significant incidents.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E002: AI failure plan for harmful outputs / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E002: AI failure plan for harmful outputs / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Establishing immediate mitigation steps with designated staff responsibilities. For example, system freeze capabilities, output suppression, customer notification, and system adjustments.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E003: AI failure plan for hallucinations / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:E003: AI failure plan for hallucinations / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Defining hallucination incident types.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E003: AI failure plan for hallucinations / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:E003: AI failure plan for hallucinations / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Coordinating potential external support. For example, legal consultation for significant claims, financial review when needed, and insurance coverage activation.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E003: AI failure plan for hallucinations / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:E003: AI failure plan for hallucinations / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E003: AI failure plan for hallucinations / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E003: AI failure plan for hallucinations / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing customer communication protocols. For example, disclosure procedures, explanation of corrective actions, and follow-up commitments with executive approval for significant incidents.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E003: AI failure plan for hallucinations / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E003: AI failure plan for hallucinations / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Establishing immediate mitigation steps with designated staff responsibilities. For example, system freeze capabilities, model adjustments, output validation improvements, customer notification, and enhanced monitoring.

nodes.label: blk:E004: Assign accountability / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Implementing code signing and verification processes for AI models, libraries, and deployment artefacts to ensure only digitally signed components are approved for production use.

nodes.label: blk:E004: Assign accountability / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Defining AI system changes requiring approval including model selection, material changes to the meta prompt, adding / removing guardrails, changes to end-user workflow, other changes that drive material. For example, +/-10% performance on evals.

nodes.label: blk:E004: Assign accountability / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Assigning an accountable lead as approver for each of these changes. Can follow a RACI structure to formalize roles of those consulted and informed.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E005: Document data storage security / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E005: Document data storage security / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Documenting data storage security. For example, assessments around cloud vs. on-premises processing.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E005: Document data storage security / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E005: Document data storage security / Control shoulds/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E006: Conduct vendor due diligence / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E006: Conduct vendor due diligence / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Defining assessment criteria for foundational or upstream AI models. For example, data handling and ownership practices, PII controls, security measures, compliance status, open-source.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E006: Conduct vendor due diligence / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E006: Conduct vendor due diligence / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Conducting documented assessments. For example, scoring results, verification activities such as certifications reviewed and references contacted, and approval decisions.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E006: Conduct vendor due diligence / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:E006: Conduct vendor due diligence / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Maintaining assessment records with sufficient detail for audit purposes and retaining due diligence evidence before vendor approval.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E006: Conduct vendor due diligence / Control shoulds/4
nodes.label: blk:E006: Conduct vendor due diligence / Control shoulds/4

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E007: [Retired] Document system change approvals / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E007: [Retired] Document system change approvals / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Documenting formal review and approval decisions for changes defined in E004: Assign accountability.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E007: [Retired] Document system change approvals / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E007: [Retired] Document system change approvals / Control shoulds/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E008: Review internal processes / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:E008: Review internal processes / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Collecting and implementing external feedback on AI systems. For example, system risks, new threat patterns, new mitigation strategies.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E008: Review internal processes / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:E008: Review internal processes / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E008: Review internal processes / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E008: Review internal processes / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Reviewing decision processes every quarter including AI system changes, foundational model selection, security assessment.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E008: Review internal processes / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E008: Review internal processes / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Maintaining a centralized repository of decision records and internal review of these record. For example, supporting evidence reviewed, remediation plans.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E008: Review internal processes / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:E008: Review internal processes / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Documenting and tracking remediation of any risks identified.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E009: Monitor third-party access / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:E009: Monitor third-party access / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Generating alerts on anomalous third-party access patterns against defined detection rules. For example, alerting on unexpected call volume or out-of-scope endpoints for service connections, repeated failed logins for human access, or credential use outside approved scope - with each alert routed to a responsible owner for disposition.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E009: Monitor third-party access / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:E009: Monitor third-party access / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E009: Monitor third-party access / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E009: Monitor third-party access / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Configuring logging for third-party interactions. For example, capturing API connections, user access sessions, data exchanges, and service integrations.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E009: Monitor third-party access / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E009: Monitor third-party access / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Capturing access metadata. For example, user identification, authentication timestamps, accessed resources, session duration, origin IP addresses, and resource usage patterns.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Real-time monitoring, blocking, or alerting capabilities.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Maintaining logging and tracking systems. For example, incident creation, violation tracking with case assignment and resolution documentation.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control mays/3
nodes.text: Conducting regular effectiveness reviews. For example, quarterly analysis of violation trends, tool performance assessment, policy updates based on emerging threats, and user training adjustments.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control mays/4
nodes.label: blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control mays/4

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Defining prohibited AI usage for end-users. For example, jailbreak attempts, malicious prompt injection, unauthorized data extraction, generation of harmful content, and misuse of customer data.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing detection and monitoring tools. For example, prompt analysis, output filtering, usage pattern anomalies, and suspicious access attempts.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:E010: Establish AI acceptable use policy / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Implementing user feedback when policy is breached. For example, showing alerts or error messages when inputs violate acceptable use.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E011: Record processing locations / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:E011: Record processing locations / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Implementing transfer compliance procedures. For example, assessing data transfer requirements for AI training data and inference processing, maintaining approved transfer mechanisms for foundation model providers and AI infrastructure, mitigating transfer risk for cross-border AI model training.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E011: Record processing locations / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:E011: Record processing locations / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E011: Record processing locations / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E011: Record processing locations / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Maintaining AI infrastructure location documentation. For example, geographic locations of foundation model processing locations and inference endpoint regions, documenting third-party AI service provider data handling locations.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E011: Record processing locations / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E011: Record processing locations / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Reviewing and updating documentation regularly.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E012: Document regulatory compliance / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E012: Document regulatory compliance / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Identifying relevant regulations. For example, data protection laws. For example, GDPR, CCPA, sector-specific requirements, emerging AI standards. For example, EU AI Act.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E012: Document regulatory compliance / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E012: Document regulatory compliance / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Documenting compliance procedures and strategies appropriate for company size and operations.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E012: Document regulatory compliance / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:E012: Document regulatory compliance / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Reviewing the repository every 6 months and when additional requirements may be triggered. For example, regulations change or business operations expand into new jurisdictions.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E012: Document regulatory compliance / Control shoulds/4
nodes.label: blk:E012: Document regulatory compliance / Control shoulds/4

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E013: Implement quality management system / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:E013: Implement quality management system / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Establishing data management and record-keeping systems. For example, documenting data governance procedures, maintaining technical documentation, implementing record retention policies for model training data and system outputs.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E013: Implement quality management system / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:E013: Implement quality management system / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Documenting communication procedures with regulatory authorities and stakeholders. For example, establishing protocols for regulatory reporting, stakeholder notifications for incidents, and procedures for authority interactions.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E013: Implement quality management system / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:E013: Implement quality management system / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E013: Implement quality management system / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E013: Implement quality management system / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Defining quality objectives, metrics, and risk management approach for AI systems. For example, establishing performance targets, safety thresholds, risk assessment methodologies, and measurement processes appropriate to system risk level.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E013: Implement quality management system / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E013: Implement quality management system / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Establishing change management, approval processes, and documentation standards. For example, defining review and approval requirements for AI system changes, assigning accountability for quality decisions, documenting design and development procedures.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E013: Implement quality management system / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:E013: Implement quality management system / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Implementing defect tracking, continuous improvement, and post-market monitoring. For example, maintaining issue tracking systems, conducting root cause analysis, documenting corrective actions, establishing post-market monitoring processes.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E014: [Retired] Share transparency reports / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:E014: [Retired] Share transparency reports / Control mays/1
nodes.text: This requirement was merged into E017 at the Q1, 2026 standard update. See aiuc-1.com/changelog for more information.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E014: [Retired] Share transparency reports / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:E014: [Retired] Share transparency reports / Control mays/2

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E015: Log AI system activity / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:E015: Log AI system activity / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Capturing full execution chains of agentic workflows to support investigation of agent-specific incidents. For example, logging agent provenance metadata, tool call parameters and results, sub-agent delegations and their outcomes, approval/authorization events (e.g., human-in-the-loop approvals), and reasoning traces where available.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E015: Log AI system activity / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:E015: Log AI system activity / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Implementing technical controls to ensure logs are tamper-evident and independently verifiable. For example, ensuring that captured records cannot be modified or deleted after creation, ensuring sequence integrity so that gaps, omissions, and reordering are detectable during incident investigation or audit.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E015: Log AI system activity / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:E015: Log AI system activity / Control mays/3

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E015: Log AI system activity / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E015: Log AI system activity / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Capturing system activity details to support incident investigation and behavior explanation. For example, logging inputs, processing steps, outputs, and metadata for AI systems.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E015: Log AI system activity / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E015: Log AI system activity / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing log storage with appropriate retention periods, access controls, and data sanitation to support auditing and incident response.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E016: Implement AI disclosure mechanisms / Control shoulds/1
nodes.label: blk:E016: Implement AI disclosure mechanisms / Control shoulds/1
nodes.text: Implementing AI disclosure for text-based interactions. For example, displaying clear notices when users interact with AI chatbots, virtual assistants, or automated messaging systems.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E016: Implement AI disclosure mechanisms / Control shoulds/2
nodes.label: blk:E016: Implement AI disclosure mechanisms / Control shoulds/2
nodes.text: Implementing AI disclosure for voice-based interactions. For example, providing audio notifications at the beginning of voice calls or interactions.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E016: Implement AI disclosure mechanisms / Control shoulds/3
nodes.label: blk:E016: Implement AI disclosure mechanisms / Control shoulds/3
nodes.text: Labelling AI-generated media and documents in a machine-readable and detectable format. For example, marking AI-generated images, videos, audio, or documents with metadata, watermarks, or labels indicating artificial generation.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E016: Implement AI disclosure mechanisms / Control shoulds/4
nodes.label: blk:E016: Implement AI disclosure mechanisms / Control shoulds/4
nodes.text: Disclosing when autonomous AI agents or systems are performing actions. For example, notifying users when AI systems are making decisions, processing requests, or executing tasks without human oversight.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E016: Implement AI disclosure mechanisms / Control shoulds/5
nodes.label: blk:E016: Implement AI disclosure mechanisms / Control shoulds/5
nodes.text: Establishing reactive disclosure capabilities when users ask if they are interacting with AI.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E016: Implement AI disclosure mechanisms / Control shoulds/6
nodes.label: blk:E016: Implement AI disclosure mechanisms / Control shoulds/6

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E017: Document system transparency policy / Control mays/1
nodes.label: blk:E017: Document system transparency policy / Control mays/1
nodes.text: Defining policies for sharing transparency documentation with external stakeholders. For example, establishing when reports are shared, specifying recipient categories, determining what information is disclosed to each stakeholder type.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E017: Document system transparency policy / Control mays/2
nodes.label: blk:E017: Document system transparency policy / Control mays/2
nodes.text: Documenting sharing procedures including approval workflows, version control, and distribution tracking. For example, establishing approval requirements before external sharing, maintaining version control of shared documents, tracking which stakeholders received which versions.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-controls:blk:E017: Document system transparency policy / Control mays/3
nodes.label: blk:E017: Document system transparency policy / Control mays/3
nodes.text: Documenting platform-level and deployer-level security responsibilities for AI systems. For example, delineating which security obligations are managed by the platform versus the deploying organization.

nodes.label: blk:E017: Document system transparency policy / Control mays/4

nodes.label: blk:E017: Document system transparency policy / Control shoulds/1

nodes.label: blk:F001: Prevent AI cyber misuse / Control mays/2

nodes.label: blk:F001: Prevent AI cyber misuse / Control shoulds/1
