nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-limitations:blk:Crosswalks are AIUC's, not this build's/1
nodes.label: blk:Crosswalks are AIUC's, not this build's/1
nodes.text:
The 1,126 crosswalk mappings to 13 external frameworks are published by AIUC. They
are reproduced with their framework, reference and text; the relationship is recorded
as published_crosswalk for exactly that reason. No mapping was inferred, extended or
scored here, and the gap and gapAnalysis fields carry whatever the source carried,
including null.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-limitations:blk:Everything else is a snapshot in time/1
nodes.label: blk:Everything else is a snapshot in time/1
nodes.text:
The catalog is what the official sources said at the retrieval timestamps in
evidence/source-manifest.json. The site is a deploying web application; it can change
between one read and the next. src/drift.py exists to tell you when it has, and
distinguishes a redeploy from a change in what the standard says. Nothing here
auto-updates.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-limitations:blk:Five differences are recorded and unresolved/1
nodes.label: blk:Five differences are recorded and unresolved/1
nodes.text:
At 2026-07-15 the website and the official repository differ in five places: three are
markdown escaping or link syntax, two are bullet order. None changes meaning, so none
blocks the release — but none has been resolved either, because resolving them means
choosing a source, and that is not this build's to choose. They are in
reports/reconciliation-latest.json.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-limitations:blk:Historical releases are thinner than the current one/1
nodes.label: blk:Historical releases are thinner than the current one/1
nodes.text:
Only the current release (2026-07-15) is built from the website, so only it carries
the published presentation metadata: mandatory/optional, frequency, control type,
keywords, capabilities, sub-controls, evidence expectations and crosswalks.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-limitations:blk:Historical releases are thinner than the current one/2
nodes.label: blk:Historical releases are thinner than the current one/2
nodes.text:
The three earlier built releases (2026-04-15, 2026-01-15, 2025-10-01) come from the
official changelog repository alone: control id, title, normative statement, and the
control shoulds and mays. They are marked partial in catalog/index.json, and that
is what partial means here. The site publishes no historical control pages, so
those fields cannot be recovered without inventing them.

nodes.label: blk:It is not the standard/1
nodes.text:
It is derived. AIUC has not reviewed it. Where it differs from
aiuc-1.com, the site is right.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-limitations:blk:One named release has no artefact/1
nodes.label: blk:One named release has no artefact/1
nodes.text:
AIUC's standard-history table names a July 22, 2025 version. No commit in the
official changelog repository survives the matching test for it, so no control set
can be traced to a source revision at that date. It is listed as unbuilt with the
reason rather than being reconstructed from the nearest commit.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-limitations:blk:Sub-control status is not stated by the source/1
nodes.label: blk:Sub-control status is not stated by the source/1
nodes.text:
AIUC-1 publishes numbered sub-controls (B006.1) with an application of Core or
Supplemental. Whether a sub-control is normative, an example, or implementation
guidance is not stated. This catalog carries them as published requirements with their
application label, and docs/source-policy.md lists this as an open question.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-limitations:blk:The announced release is not built/1
nodes.label: blk:The announced release is not built/1
nodes.text:
The changelog page announces October 15, 2026. Announced is not published: it is
recorded in catalog/index.json as announced with the sentence that announced it,
and has no artefact.

nodes.label: blk:Anchor nodes/1
nodes.text:
An external clause is an anchor node in the sense that document gives the term: well
connected, maintained by someone else, well known, and carrying no authority here. There
are 489 of them. Nothing in this vault says a control is an article; the edges say a
control's text and an article's text share these words, and AIUC publishes a crosswalk
between them, and those are two different claims kept apart.

nodes.label: blk:Anchor nodes/2
nodes.text:
Where an EU AI Act anchor names an article, it also carries a pointer to the estate's
Regulation Graph vault, where Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 is parsed from official Formex
XML and hash-verified. That pointer is a reference, not an assertion about the article.

nodes.label: blk:Reading it/1
nodes.text: graph/meaning/index.json — the grades, the counts, every anchor, every bridging term.

nodes.label: blk:Reading it/2
nodes.text: graph/meaning/controls/<id>.json — one control's evidence and candidates in full.

nodes.label: blk:Reading it/3
nodes.text:
graph/meaning/edges.json — every edge with its grade and the sentence that says what it
  asserts.

nodes.label: blk:Reading it/4
nodes.text: graph/docs/<slug>/ — the decomposition each of those edges points into.

nodes.label: blk:Reading it/5
nodes.text:
Or open the vault's own page: a control's panel shows the shared words and the gap, and the
graph explorer walks any of it one degree at a time.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-meaning:blk:The gap is the honest half/1
nodes.label: blk:The gap is the honest half/1
nodes.text:
For every published crosswalk this build reports two lists: the distinctive terms the two
texts share, and the distinctive terms the clause holds that the control never uses. The
second list is the interesting one. It is where the mapping is doing work that the wording
does not show.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-meaning:blk:The gap is the honest half/2
nodes.label: blk:The gap is the honest half/2
nodes.text:
257 of the 1,126 crosswalks AIUC publishes share no distinctive vocabulary at all. That
is not an error and it is not a criticism. It means AIUC mapped those on meaning rather than
on words, which is what a human crosswalk is for. Recording it makes the difference between
the two kinds of mapping visible instead of averaged away.

nodes.label: blk:The three grades, never mixed/1
nodes.text:
| Grade | What it means | How it was arrived at |
|---|---|---|
| **structural** | Read from the sources. Exact, no judgement. | A section of `controls.md` headed `A001: …` states control A001. A paragraph that is character-for-character a requirement's published text is that requirement's wording. |
| **published** | AIUC publishes this crosswalk. The vocabulary evidence is this build's. | For each control-to-clause mapping AIUC publishes, which distinctive words the two texts share, and which of the clause's distinctive words the control never reaches. |
| **proposed** | This build's candidate. Not AIUC's, and not a mapping. | A control and a clause AIUC has **not** crosswalked share distinctive vocabulary. Recorded with `review_status: needs_review`. |

nodes.label: blk:The three grades, never mixed/2
nodes.text:
Every edge in graph/meaning/edges.json carries its grade. Nothing downstream treats a
proposal as a mapping, and the app marks a proposal on every surface it appears on.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-meaning:blk:What a term is, and why rarity decides/1
nodes.label: blk:What a term is, and why rarity decides/1
nodes.text:
A term here is a stem, not a word: agent, agents and agent's are one term. The stemmer
is deliberately shallow and stated rather than clever, in src/terms.py, because a stem is
an internal key and the words as written travel with it.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-meaning:blk:What a term is, and why rarity decides/2
nodes.label: blk:What a term is, and why rarity decides/2
nodes.text:
A term is only evidence if it is rare. data appears in hundreds of clauses and says
nothing about which clause a control is about; jailbreak appears in a handful and says a
great deal. Each term is scored by inverse document frequency across the corpus of 489
distinct external clauses plus the 53 control texts, normalised to 0–1, and only terms above
a floor count as evidence. The score for a control-to-clause pair answers a specific
question — *how much of that clause's distinctive vocabulary does this control's text
reach? — rather than the vaguer do these look alike*.

nodes.label: blk:What this does not do/1
nodes.text: It does not propose a mapping AIUC should adopt. A candidate is a reason to look.

nodes.label: blk:What this does not do/2
nodes.text:
It does not score how compliant anything is. There is no such number here and there
  will not be.

nodes.label: blk:What this does not do/3
nodes.text:
It does not resolve the 257 wordless crosswalks. Resolving one means deciding what AIUC
  meant, which is not this build's to decide.

nodes.label: blk:What this does not do/4
nodes.text:
It does not stem cleverly. authorization and authorizing land on different stems, and
  that inflates a shared count slightly. The terms as written are shown, so a reader can see
  it happening.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-meaning:blk:Why the paragraph had to be nailed down first/1
nodes.label: blk:Why the paragraph had to be nailed down first/1
nodes.text:
An edge to a paragraph is worth what the paragraph's identity is worth. So before any
meaning was added, every source document was decomposed with the estate's own
gen_coregraph — document, section, block, sentence, word, plus a formatting graph and an
identity ledger — and the gate that matters ran on each: **the markdown rebuilds from its
formatting graph byte-identical to its source**. Every document in the vault, every
paragraph in them, reversible.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-meaning:blk:Why the paragraph had to be nailed down first/2
nodes.label: blk:Why the paragraph had to be nailed down first/2
nodes.text:
That is what makes blk:A006: Prevent PII leakage / Control shoulds/1 a thing you can
point at rather than a line number that moves.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-meaning:blk:Why the paragraph had to be nailed down first/3
nodes.label: blk:Why the paragraph had to be nailed down first/3
nodes.text:
The counts live in graph/docs/index.json and are deliberately not repeated here: this
file is one of the documents being counted, so quoting its own totals would make them wrong
the moment anyone edits it.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-methodology:blk:1. Discovery, from the site's own model/1
nodes.label: blk:1. Discovery, from the site's own model/1
nodes.text:
The AIUC-1 site is a React application that ships its published control model in
the page payload: domains, controls, sub-controls, evidence expectations, keywords,
crosswalks. src/discover_sources.py reads that model out of the home page rather
than scraping rendered HTML, and writes evidence/discovery-manifest.json.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-methodology:blk:1. Discovery, from the site's own model/2
nodes.label: blk:1. Discovery, from the site's own model/2
nodes.text:
Nothing is hardcoded. There is no control list in the code. A control that stops
being published stops being discovered, and the inventory check in src/validate.py
notices the difference against the previous release.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-methodology:blk:1. Discovery, from the site's own model/3
nodes.label: blk:1. Discovery, from the site's own model/3
nodes.text:
A second hop reads the changelog page for the per-release changelog pages it links
to, so historical releases are discovered rather than assumed.

nodes.label: blk:2. Capture, politely/1
nodes.text: src/fetch_sources.py is the only place bytes enter the build.

nodes.label: blk:2. Capture, politely/2
nodes.text: One request per second per host, an explicit user agent naming this build.

nodes.label: blk:2. Capture, politely/3
nodes.text:
robots.txt fetched and honoured; if it cannot be retrieved at all, the fetcher
  refuses to fetch rather than assuming permission.

nodes.label: blk:2. Capture, politely/4
nodes.text: Conditional requests when a prior snapshot carries an ETag.

nodes.label: blk:2. Capture, politely/5
nodes.text: Bounded exponential backoff, transient status codes only.

nodes.label: blk:2. Capture, politely/6
nodes.text:
The exact received body saved gzipped under evidence/snapshots/<day>/<ref>.html.gz,
  with an observation recording the final URL, status, content type, retrieval time
  and SHA-256.

nodes.label: blk:3. Extraction, structurally/1
nodes.text:
src/rsc.py reads the payload format the site publishes: rows, length-prefixed
text rows, and references of the form $<row>:<path>. Two behaviours matter:

nodes.label: blk:3. Extraction, structurally/2
nodes.text:
Pruning before expansion. Each control carries a back-reference to its domain,
  which carries every control. Following it is unbounded, so it is dropped: the
  parent is known from context.

nodes.label: blk:3. Extraction, structurally/3
nodes.text:
Self-references resolved against the model itself. Repeated objects — crosswalk
  clauses above all — are published once and referenced by path afterwards. Those
  paths are walked against the control model rather than the whole page.

nodes.label: blk:3. Extraction, structurally/4
nodes.text:
src/parse_pages.py then reads each control from its own page, not only from the
home-page index, and compares the two. All 53 controls in the current release are
confirmed by their own page; any that were not would be marked needs_review.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-methodology:blk:4. History, from the official repository/1
nodes.label: blk:4. History, from the official repository/1
nodes.text:
src/parse_changelog.py reads every commit in aiunderwriting/AIUC-1-Changelog
that touches standard/, capturing the blob SHA, the SHA-256 and the parsed content
of controls.md and requirements.md at that commit, and reads the official
changelog pages for the release dates and the published change table.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-methodology:blk:5. Matching a commit to a release, explicitly/1
nodes.label: blk:5. Matching a commit to a release, explicitly/1
nodes.text:
The repository was created after the first releases and backfills them in order, so
commit date is not the signal. src/release_sources.py matches on the commit subject
naming the release month, rules out a subject naming a different day, and takes the
earliest unmatched commit. Every match records its rationale and a confidence (0.95
when the subject names the published day, 0.85 when it names only the month). The
2025-07-22 release has no commit that survives that test, so it is recorded as
unbuilt with the reason, rather than being given the nearest commit.

nodes.label: blk:6. Normalisation, without overwriting/1
nodes.text:
src/normalize_catalog.py builds the control records. Every mapped value sits beside
the source wording it came from:

nodes.label: blk:6. Normalisation, without overwriting/2
blk:6. Normalisation, without overwriting/3
nodes.text:
A label with no unambiguous mapping produces {"value": null, "raw_text": "..."} and
a finding. Sub-control descriptions carry one or more source bullets; they are split
on the bullet marker and kept verbatim alongside the whole description.

nodes.label: blk:7. Reconciliation/1
nodes.text:
src/reconcile.py compares the website's control set with the repository's markdown
at the matched commit: titles, statements, and the bullet sets. Differences are
classified:

nodes.label: blk:7. Reconciliation/2
nodes.text: title_conflict, summary_conflict, guidance_set_conflict — blocking;

nodes.label: blk:7. Reconciliation/3
nodes.text:
guidance_order_difference, guidance_formatting_difference — recorded, not
  blocking, and each says why it is not.

nodes.label: blk:7. Reconciliation/4
nodes.text:
At the 2026-07-15 release there are five findings, none blocking: three are markdown
escaping or a link written as markdown on one side and plain text on the other, two
are the same bullets in a different order.

nodes.label: blk:8. The graph/1
nodes.text:
src/build_graph.py decomposes the catalog into nodes and edges. Seventeen edge
kinds, each with the sentence that says what it means, in graph/index.json. The
point is the same one this estate keeps arriving at: a control's properties are just
words, and what it is shows in the edges traceable from it — its domain, its
requirements, the evidence each expects, the external clauses it is crosswalked to,
the release it appeared in, the commit that carries it and the page it was read from.

nodes.label: blk:9. The gate/1
nodes.text:
src/validate.py runs four levels — schema, source traceability, semantic, and
inventory. A release may only say validated when all four pass and no blocking
reconciliation finding exists. tests/run.py runs the schema gate and the
traceability gate red on purpose, because a validator that has never failed is
not known to work.

nodes.label: blk:Contact/1
nodes.text:
If you are AIUC and want something here changed or removed, the fastest route is the
sgit.ai project behind <https://graphs.sgit.ai>. Removal will be honoured.

nodes.label: blk:How the sources were used/1
nodes.text:
Public pages were retrieved with an explicit user agent identifying this build, at
most one request per second, honouring robots.txt (the site served no robots file
at capture time; the manifest records that observation). No authentication was used,
no private content was accessed, and no URL was guessed: every page fetched was
linked from a page already fetched.

nodes.label: blk:How the sources were used/2
nodes.text:
Retrieved bytes are retained inside this vault as gzipped snapshots so a reader can
check a claim against what was actually received. They are evidence, not a mirror.
Extracted control wording is reproduced here for verification; **reuse rights for
the full control text have not been confirmed with AIUC**, and anyone republishing
this catalog publicly should confirm them first — docs/source-policy.md records
this as an open question, and the source manifest carries the same note on every
observation.

nodes.label: blk:The official sources/1
nodes.text:
| Source | What it is canonical for |
|---|---|
| <https://www.aiuc-1.com/> | the current public control text and its published presentation metadata |
| <https://www.aiuc-1.com/changelog> | the official release dates and release narrative |
| <https://github.com/aiunderwriting/AIUC-1-Changelog> | the official record of what changed between releases |

nodes.label: blk:The official sources/2
nodes.text: If anything here disagrees with those, those are right and this is wrong.

nodes.label: blk:What this is not/1
nodes.text: It is not approved, certified, endorsed or reviewed by AIUC.

nodes.label: blk:What this is not/2
nodes.text: It is not an official AIUC API, export or data feed.

nodes.label: blk:What this is not/3
nodes.text: It is not a substitute for the standard. The official sources are canonical.

nodes.label: blk:What this is not/4
nodes.text:
It makes no compliance, certification, underwriting, insurance, legal, privacy
  or security claim about anybody, and cannot be used to make one.

nodes.label: blk:What this is/1
nodes.text:
aiuc-1 is an unofficial, derivative, machine-readable representation of the
public AIUC-1 standard, produced by the sgit.ai graph estate.

nodes.label: blk:Building it/1
nodes.text:
```bash
python3 src/build.py        # the whole chain, in order, ending at the gate
python3 tests/run.py        # 11 tests, two of which run the gates red on purpose
python3 src/drift.py        # re-fetch and report drift against the recorded manifest
```

nodes.label: blk:Building it/2
nodes.text:
The chain is: discover_sources → fetch_sources → parse_pages →
parse_changelog → normalize_catalog → diff_releases → build_docgraph →
build_meaning → build_graph → validate. Each stage runs on its own; src/build.py runs them in order.

nodes.label: blk:Building it/3
nodes.text:
Rebuilds are reproducible, with one honest caveat: the artefacts carry the run's own
timestamps, so two runs differ in those fields. Pin the clock and they do not:

nodes.label: blk:Building it/4
nodes.text:
```bash
SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1788214000 python3 src/build.py    # byte-stable from the same snapshots
```

nodes.label: blk:Building it/5
nodes.text:
The content_hash on every release and the normalized_content_hash on every control
are computed over the substance and not the timestamps, so they are stable either way —
that is what makes them worth comparing.

nodes.label: blk:Licence and attribution/1
nodes.text:
The AIUC-1 content quoted, hashed and linked here belongs to AIUC. See NOTICE.md.
The build code in src/ and the schemas in schemas/ are part of the sgit.ai graph
estate and carry that estate's licence (CC BY 4.0 for content, see the parent
repository).

nodes.label: blk:The layout/1
nodes.text:
```
catalog/        current.json, index.json, releases/<release-id>.json
sources/        the official markdown at the release commit, as it was decomposed
graph/          nodes.json, edges.json, index.json (the edge vocabulary and its meanings)
  docs/         one folder per source document: the core graph, the formatting graph,
                the identity ledger, the token analysis
  meaning/      the anchors, the terms, and the graded edges between them
changes/        <release-id>.json — derived change events and the official change rows
evidence/       source-manifest.json, discovery-manifest.json, snapshots/<day>/<ref>.html.gz
                (the snapshots live in the vault, not in the public repository — see below)
reports/        validation-latest.json, reconciliation-latest.json, drift-latest.json
schemas/        the five JSON Schemas every artefact is validated against
src/            the build chain, one module per stage
docs/           methodology, source policy, review workflow, limitations
tests/          fixture-based parser tests and red tests for the gates
```

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-readme:blk:The rules this build holds to/1
nodes.label: blk:The rules this build holds to/1
nodes.text:
Evidence, not compliance. Nothing here says an organisation passes, fails,
   or is certified. It says what the published standard says, and where.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-readme:blk:The rules this build holds to/2
nodes.label: blk:The rules this build holds to/2
nodes.text:
Every claim names its source. A non-null canonical field carries at least one
   source reference; every reference resolves to an observation with a URL, a
   retrieval timestamp and a content hash. The gate fails otherwise.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-readme:blk:The rules this build holds to/3
nodes.label: blk:The rules this build holds to/3
nodes.text:
Conflicts are preserved, not resolved. Where the website and the official
   changelog repository disagree, both readings are kept and the difference is
   recorded. A difference that changes meaning is blocking; one that is only
   markdown escaping or bullet order is not, and says which it is.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-readme:blk:The rules this build holds to/4
nodes.label: blk:The rules this build holds to/4
nodes.text:
Nothing is invented. An enum exists only where the source publishes a label
   that maps unambiguously. Anything else is null beside its raw text, with a
   finding attached.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-readme:blk:The rules this build holds to/5
nodes.label: blk:The rules this build holds to/5
nodes.text:
A connection this build proposed says so. Structural edges are read from the
   sources; published crosswalks are AIUC's; a candidate this build noticed is graded
   proposed and marked needs_review on every surface it appears on. docs/meaning.md
   is the whole story.

nodes.id: docblk:aiuc1-readme:blk:The rules this build holds to/6
nodes.label: blk:The rules this build holds to/6
nodes.text:
The parser fails closed. If a page stops yielding the model this build reads,
   the run opens a review item rather than emitting a guess.

nodes.label: blk:The terminology inversion, stated once/1
nodes.text:
AIUC-1 calls a top-level item a requirement (A001) and its numbered children
controls (A001.1). The brief this catalog was built to calls the top-level item
a control and its children requirements. This catalog follows the brief, and
every control record carries source_terminology saying what the site calls it, so
the inversion is visible rather than silent.

nodes.label: blk:What is here/1
nodes.text:
| | |
|---|---|
| **5 releases** | 2025-10-01, 2026-01-15, 2026-04-15, 2026-07-15 built; 2025-07-22 named by AIUC but carrying no commit, so unbuilt and recorded as such |
| **53 controls** | in the current release (2026-07-15), across 6 domains |
| **144 requirements** | the numbered sub-controls, each with the evidence it expects |
| **1,126 crosswalks** | published mappings to 13 external frameworks, the EU AI Act among them |
| **194 change events** | derived from release-to-release differences, plus 104 change rows AIUC publishes itself |
| **1,238 nodes, 3,526 edges** | the whole thing as one graph |
| **82 source observations** | one per captured page, each with its URL, retrieval time, content hash and retained snapshot |
| **9 documents to the word** | every source markdown decomposed to document, section, paragraph, sentence, word, each rebuilding byte-identical from its formatting graph. The counts are in `graph/docs/index.json`, and they move whenever this file does — which is why they are not repeated here |
| **489 anchors, 357 bridging terms** | the external clauses as anchor nodes, and the distinctive vocabulary that carries a control out to them |

nodes.label: blk:What is here/2
nodes.text:
Numbers are the build's own, from catalog/index.json, graph/index.json and
evidence/source-manifest.json. They are computed, not remembered: rerun
python3 src/build.py and read them again.

nodes.label: blk:Where the bytes live/1
nodes.text:
The retained response bodies — one gzipped copy of every page this catalog was read
from — are in the vault, under evidence/snapshots/, and are deliberately not in
the public git repository. They are copies of someone else's pages, and NOTICE.md is
explicit that reuse rights for that content have not been confirmed with AIUC.

nodes.label: blk:Where the bytes live/2
nodes.text:
What the repository does carry is every snapshot's path and SHA-256, in
evidence/source-manifest.json. So the chain holds either way: a reader with the
vault can check a claim against the bytes; a reader with only the repository can check
that the hash of those bytes is the one the catalog was built from.

nodes.label: blk:The loop/1
nodes.text: A scheduled src/drift.py run re-fetches every discovered page and the repository.

nodes.label: blk:The loop/2
nodes.text: It classifies each difference as known (presentation only) or unknown.

nodes.label: blk:The loop/3
nodes.text:
Every unknown difference becomes a review item, and its snapshot is retained;
   snapshots for known differences are discarded, because nothing was learned.

nodes.label: blk:The loop/4
nodes.text:
A human reads the retained snapshot beside the recorded one — both are complete
   response bodies, so they can be diffed.

nodes.label: blk:The loop/5
nodes.text:
An approved correction becomes either a deterministic parser rule or an explicit
   recorded override. It never becomes a hand-edited catalog file.

nodes.label: blk:The loop/6
nodes.text:
src/build.py reruns; src/validate.py decides whether the release may say
   validated.

nodes.label: blk:The rule about language models/1
nodes.text:
A language model may propose a label, explain what changed between two snapshots, or
draft a test. It is never the authority for a normative value. Every canonical
field in this catalog is grounded in captured official text and a deterministic
check, and the gate enforces that independently of how a value was proposed.

nodes.label: blk:What a review item carries/1
nodes.text:
```json
{
  "review_id": "rev_2026_08_31_src_2026_08_31_control_b006",
  "opened_at": "<timestamp>",
  "affected": "<source ref, control id or field>",
  "url": "<official page>",
  "kind": "content_change",
  "reason": "<why this could not be decided automatically>",
  "parser_version": "0.1.0",
  "proposed_value": null,
  "reviewer": null,
  "decided_at": null,
  "rationale": null,
  "status": "open"
}
```

nodes.label: blk:What a review item carries/2
nodes.text:
Open items live in reports/review-queue.json; the run that opened them is in
reports/drift-latest.json.

nodes.label: blk:What opens a review item/1
nodes.text:
A drift run finds a page whose published control model changed (a change in raw
  bytes alone is classified as a site deploy and does not).

nodes.label: blk:What opens a review item/2
nodes.text: A page stops yielding a control model — the parser fails closed.

nodes.label: blk:What opens a review item/3
nodes.text: The official changelog repository has a commit the catalog was not built from.

nodes.label: blk:What opens a review item/4
nodes.text: A source label appears that no mapping table covers.

nodes.label: blk:What opens a review item/5
nodes.text: The website and the official repository disagree in a way that changes meaning.

nodes.label: blk:The open question about redistribution/1
nodes.text:
Reuse rights for the full AIUC-1 control text have not been confirmed with AIUC.
This catalog reproduces control wording so a reader can verify what was extracted.
Before publishing this content anywhere public, confirm with AIUC whether:

nodes.label: blk:The open question about redistribution/2
nodes.text: full control text may be republished, or only metadata, hashes and source links;

nodes.label: blk:The open question about redistribution/3
nodes.text:
an official export or API exists or is planned, so that this could become a
   supported integration rather than a derived catalog;

nodes.label: blk:The open question about redistribution/4
nodes.text: the website's control URLs are intended to be stable permalinks;

nodes.label: blk:The open question about redistribution/5
blk:The open question about redistribution/6
nodes.text: what attribution, caching and redistribution terms apply.

nodes.label: blk:The open question about redistribution/7
nodes.text:
Until those are answered, the honest position is the one NOTICE.md takes: this is
evidence with a chain of custody, not a mirror, and removal will be honoured on
request.

nodes.label: blk:What is retained/1
nodes.text:
Gzipped copies of the exact response bodies, inside the vault, under
evidence/snapshots/<day>/. They exist so a reader can check a claim against the
bytes rather than trusting this build. A drift run keeps a new snapshot only where
the extracted model actually changed.

nodes.label: blk:What was retrieved, and how/1
nodes.text:
User agent: `sgit-ai-aiuc1-catalog/<version> (+https://graphs.sgit.ai; derived
  machine-readable catalog; contact via graphs.sgit.ai)`.

nodes.label: blk:What was retrieved, and how/2
nodes.text: Rate: at most one request per second per host.

nodes.label: blk:What was retrieved, and how/3
nodes.text:
robots.txt: fetched before any page. At capture time https://www.aiuc-1.com/robots.txt
  answered HTTP 404, so there were no directives to honour; the manifest records that
  observation verbatim rather than the conclusion alone.

nodes.label: blk:What was retrieved, and how/4
nodes.text:
No authentication, no private endpoints, no non-public APIs, no slug guessing. Every
  page fetched was linked from a page already fetched.

nodes.label: blk:What was retrieved, and how/5
nodes.text: The GitHub repository was read as a public git clone.

nodes.label: blk:Which source wins/1
nodes.text:
| Question | Source |
|---|---|
| What does the standard say now? | the website |
| What did it say before? | the official changelog repository |
| When was a release published? | the official changelog page's own statement |
| What changed in a release? | the official changelog page's change table, kept verbatim and separate from anything derived |

nodes.label: blk:Which source wins/2
nodes.text:
Where the website and the repository disagree, neither wins. Both readings are
preserved, the difference is classified, and a difference that changes meaning stops
the release being published as validated.
